title: VISBIAS: Measuring Explicit and Implicit Social Biases in Vision Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model predictions on explicit multiple-choice and yes-no questions (e.g., estimating income and education) from human images, analyzing word frequencies and sentiment in image descriptions, and measuring attribute distribution shifts in implicit form completion tasks.

Evaluating model predictions on explicit multiple-choice and yes-no questions from human images of different racial groups, analyzing stereotypic word frequencies and sentiment in image descriptions, and measuring attribute distribution shifts in implicit form completion tasks.
Assessing model associations between specific demographic groups and religions using explicit multiple-choice questions, and measuring distribution shifts in implicit form completion tasks.

Testing explicit multiple-choice and yes-no questions comparing individuals' perceived annual income, education levels, and occupations based on visual demographic cues, as well as tracking attribute correlations in form completion tasks.
Evaluating explicit multiple-choice questions that ask models to guess political leanings based on demographic appearance, and measuring correlations in the form completion task.
Measuring stereotypic correlations (e.g., associating specific sexual orientations with certain personality types) by calculating distribution shifts in the implicit form completion task.
Measuring attribute distribution shifts and stereotypic correlations when conditioning on disability status in the implicit form completion task.
Measuring attribute distribution shifts and correlations when conditioning on different age categories in the implicit form completion task.
